headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth powers can amplify ACI’s CRM/email outputs into leakage, conflicts, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can ingest and emit content through email, Slack, Notion, Sheets, CRM, and MCP, while Devin can consume MCP/server outputs and act autonomously in a cloud workspace. A shared channel exists, so attacker-controlled content from ACI can plausibly steer Devin unless provenance is enforced. This is not proven by docs, so uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF ACI forwards untrusted email/CRM/Slack content into MCP or files that Devin reads, injection is plausible.
IF Devin treats ACI-produced text as instructions without provenance checks, hijack risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all ACI outputs before Devin reads them.
Restrict Devin to a read-only queue for ACI-generated artifacts.
Require a human approval step for any Devin action triggered by ACI text.
Disable MCP handoff between the two agents unless explicitly needed.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches lead generation, customer support, calendar, email, CRM, and research data, and Devin has broad network egress plus write access to cloud workspace files and integrations. If ACI passes sensitive records into Devin’s workspace, Devin can transmit them to third-party APIs or shared integrations. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default-style deployments, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ACI places CRM/email/calendar data into files or messages Devin can read, leakage becomes possible.
IF Devin uses its default integrations or network egress on those artifacts, data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep ACI customer data out of shared files and shared chat threads.
Use a redaction step before any ACI output reaches Devin.
Disable Devin network egress for tasks involving ACI data.
Separate OAuth principals for ACI and Devin integrations.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention policies between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ACI can call APIs and run via MCP, while Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP with parallel sessions. Both can mutate shared external resources such as Slack, Notion, and GitHub-like integrations, so concurrent writes can collide and overwrite each other. The overlap is broad and default-dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repo, Slack thread, Notion page, or ticket, write conflicts can occur.
IF parallel sessions are enabled for Devin while ACI also writes the same resource, race conditions are likely.
mitigations: Assign separate ownership of each shared resource to only one agent at a time.
Use branch-per-agent and merge only after review.
Lock shared tickets/pages before either agent edits them.
Disable parallel Devin sessions for overlapping tasks.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared integrations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM, email, and research outputs that Devin can then act on through GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or shell/browser tools. Devin is autonomous and long-running, so if it treats ACI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, messages, or workflow actions. The pair therefore has a strong default pathway from generated content to downstream action.
conditions: IF Devin consumes ACI-produced summaries without verification, mistaken facts can propagate.
IF Devin is allowed to commit, message, or ticket based on ACI output, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
mitigations: Require Devin to cite source artifacts before acting on ACI output.
Add a human review gate for any outward-facing action.
Limit Devin to drafting, not sending or committing, when fed ACI content.
Have ACI output structured data with confidence fields and provenance.
requires-engineering: implement verification against original records before action.

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles email, CRM, calendar, and customer support data, while Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs with broad cloud-workspace access. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes differ and both have external integrations, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF ACI customer data is routed into Devin-managed issue trackers or docs, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF either agent stores regulated customer data in its default integrations, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared tickets and docs.
Review retention settings on Slack, Notion, Jira, and GitHub integrations.
Use separate workspaces for customer data and engineering tasks.
Document a data-class-to-tool mapping for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
